solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Blunder ignoring second fall

indicators.note: ignoring means the letter for second is left out of the word for blunder

parts.note: to blunder is to stumble

explanation.surface: Someone makes a gaffe and takes a tumble, but not for the second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe dropping suddenly to the ground; a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Note convict in early part of week getting guidance

indicators.note: in tells us the note and convict sit inside the abbreviated weekday

parts.note: TUE is the usual short form of Tuesday, early in the week
TE is a note of the sol-fa scale
LAG is slang for a convict, as in old lag

explanation.surface: A prisoner receives a note early in the week offering advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is instruction or protection given by a tutor or guardian, a synonym of guidance.

clue.text: Race with graduate before short judge, titled figure

indicators.note: before places the shortened judge ahead of the titled figure

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word for judge is dropped

parts.note: to judge is to rate
HON, short for Honourable, is a title given to certain nobles

explanation.surface: A race featuring a graduate, a judge and an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon is a long-distance running race of about 26 miles.

clue.text: One's informed when kept in such facilities before parking

definitions.text: One's informed when kept in such

parts.note: LOO is British slang for a toilet, the facilities
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone learns things while stuck in the toilets before going to the car park.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the idiom: to be kept in the loop is to be kept informed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the loop is the idiom for being kept up to date, so the definition describes the circle you are kept within.

clue.text: On reflection, suitable Irish record followed by a drink

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirror-wise, so the whole string is read backwards
followed by puts the a at the end of the string before it is turned round

parts.note: fit means suitable
EP, an extended-play disc, is a record

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about a fitting Irish record and then has a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' turns all of FITIREPA backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: Absurd purpose store devised

indicators.note: devised suggests the letters are worked out into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone thinks the reason a shop was set up is ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: Preposterous means contrary to reason or common sense, a synonym of absurd.

clue.text: Poor crop yield internally revealed

indicators.note: internally revealed means the answer is found inside the words crop yield

explanation.surface: A farmer finds an inside report showing the harvest was bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropy is informal British for poor in quality or in health.

clue.text: Hot gossip brought up about Oscar winner's latest character

indicators.note: about means the reversed gossip goes round the next pieces
in a down clue, brought up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: dirt is scandalous gossip
O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: latest character means the last letter of the word winner's

explanation.surface: Juicy gossip surfaces concerning the personality of a recent Academy Award winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns DIRT into TRID, which goes about O and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrid means very hot and dry, as in torrid heat.

clue.text: Fine linked to being dishonest in high-level activity?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
lying is being dishonest

explanation.surface: A penalty is attached to dishonesty in some top-level role.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: flying is literally done at a high level.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying takes place up in the air, so it is humorously an activity at a high level.

clue.text: Wild trout concealing bass and other fish

indicators.note: concealing means the rearranged letters hide the bass inside them
wild suggests the letters run free into a new order

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bass in music

explanation.surface: A wild trout hides a bass and other fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges TROUT as TUROT, which conceals B.
explanation.definitionFit: The turbot is a large flatfish, a different fish from those named in the surface.

clue.text: Cat left out in front of joiner's yard is a risk

indicators.note: in means the shortened cat goes inside the other letters
front of means the first letter of joiner's
out means the letter for left is removed

parts.note: the leopard is a big cat

explanation.surface: A big cat abandoned in front of a carpenter's yard poses a danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the shortened cat between the J (front of joiner's) and Y; 'joiner's yard' reads as a carpenter's workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeopardy is danger of loss or harm, a synonym of risk.

clue.text: Institution of elementary significance?

parts.note: elementary seems to mean basic or trivial, but here it means providing the first stage of education

explanation.surface: Something is mocked as an organisation of only basic importance.
explanation.walkthrough: An infant school is a British school for children aged about four to seven, the very first stage of elementary education.
explanation.definitionFit: The school educates the youngest pupils, so it is literally an establishment for elementary learning.

clue.text: Departed very happy having got rid of outsiders

indicators.note: got rid of outsiders means the first and last letters of the synonym are dropped

parts.note: elated means very happy

explanation.surface: Someone is overjoyed after ejecting a few intruders.
explanation.definitionFit: Late is used of a person who has died, a polite sense of departed.

clue.text: Diplomat showing empty jealousy?

indicators.note: showing here means the word for jealousy displays the empty symbol within it

parts.note: envy is a form of jealousy
O, the zero figure, represents empty or nothing

explanation.surface: An ambassador displays hollow envy.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy is a messenger or representative sent by a government, a kind of diplomat.

clue.text: Indicate mathematical function for audience

indicators.note: for audience means the word is spoken to listeners, so its sound counts

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A teacher points out a maths function to the class.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign is to signal or show something, a synonym of indicate.

clue.text: Horrify a leading Christian convert, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is judged by how it sounds

parts.note: St Paul, converted on the road to Damascus, is a leading Christian convert

explanation.surface: Someone dismays a prominent convert to Christianity, rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Paul' said aloud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to fill someone with horror or dismay.

clue.text: Moment judge faces suspect

indicators.note: faces means stands in front of the next piece

parts.note: iffy means suspect or dubious

explanation.surface: A brief moment as a judge looks at the accused.
explanation.definitionFit: A jiffy is informal for a very short time, as in back in a jiffy.

clue.text: A coup after power's lost trapping defective military authority

indicators.note: defective suggests the letters are faulty and must be reassembled
lost means the letter for power drops out of the word trapping

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: After a coup, a military regime falls when its leader's power goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes one P from TRAPPING, giving TRAPING; 'defective' rearranges A COUP plus TRAPING.
explanation.definitionFit: A group captain is a senior RAF officer, a figure of military authority.

clue.text: Flower comes from around about a mile, cultivated across lake

parts.note: CA, for circa, means around or about

indicators.note: across means the rearranged letters span either side of the lake
cultivated suggests the letters are worked like soil into a new form

explanation.surface: A flower grows about a mile away, cultivated over by the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' turns A MILE into MELIA, which goes across L.
explanation.definitionFit: The camellia is a flowering evergreen shrub prized for its blooms.

clue.text: Rota yet to change to accommodate new legal type

indicators.note: to accommodate means the anagram takes the next letter inside
change means the letters of rota yet are altered in order

explanation.surface: A duty roster is about to be revised to fit in a new lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges ROTAYET as ATTOREY, which accommodates N.
explanation.definitionFit: An attorney is a lawyer, especially in the US, a type of legal professional.

clue.text: Plain substance smelly cat dislodged

parts.note: matter is physical substance
off means gone bad and smelly, of food

indicators.note: dislodged means the letters of cat are knocked out of place

explanation.surface: Something ordinary, smelly stuff a cat has knocked loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter-of-fact means unemotional and straightforward, which is a sense of plain.

clue.text: Smart salesman getting flat when promoted

indicators.note: promoted means raised up, so in a down clue the pieces read upwards

parts.note: REP is short for a sales representative
PAD is slang for a flat or home

explanation.surface: A salesman gets an apartment when he is given a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Dapper means neat and trim in appearance, a sense of smart.

clue.text: Like a leading person, English, in unconventional choir

indicators.note: in means the letter for English is placed inside the anagram
unconventional suggests the letters are in a non-standard order

explanation.surface: An Englishman sings in an unorthodox choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unconventional' rearranges CHOIR as HROIC, with E in.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading man or woman is the hero of a story, and heroic means like a hero.

clue.text: Top chap expected? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the words chap expected is used

explanation.surface: A man predicts the summit, but only in part.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or tip of something, a synonym of top.

clue.text: Locks feature in this river surrounded by slime

indicators.note: surrounded by means the river letter is enclosed by the slime word

parts.note: scum is a layer of slime or dirt

explanation.surface: Canal locks appear on this river, which is choked with slime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' suggests canals, but in rugby the locks are forwards who play in the second row of the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the locks are second-row forwards who push within the set piece.

clue.text: Very old film attracting old ban

parts.note: ET is the famous Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A very old movie attracts an old prohibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very old film' reads as one phrase, but VERY gives V and the second 'old' gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is a formal prohibition or rejection of a proposal, so it acts as a ban.

clue.text: Collapse in congregation?

definitions.meaning: to collapse or give way, as a business does
a church congregation is a flock

explanation.definitionFit: Fold means to give way as a failing firm does, and also a flock or body of believers.

clue.text: Neighbour prioritising time for forbidden activity

indicators.note: prioritising means putting the letter for time first

parts.note: to neighbour is to abut, lie next to

explanation.surface: The person next door puts time first before doing something not allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving T of ABUT to the front gives the variant spelling of taboo.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, something prohibited by custom.

clue.text: Poor clot violated etiquette

indicators.note: violated suggests the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A hapless idiot breaches proper manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocol is the formal code of conduct for official occasions, a kind of etiquette.

clue.text: Measure taken in old ship after European disembarks

indicators.note: disembarks means the European gets off, leaving the ship

parts.note: a galleon is an old sailing ship

explanation.surface: A measure taken aboard an old ship after a European goes ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallon is a unit of liquid volume, a standard measure.

clue.text: College had to be demolished in part in Northern town

indicators.note: in means the anagram goes inside the word for part

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

indicators.note: to be demolished means knocked down and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A college is partly scheduled for demolition in a town in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'College had' looks like the subject of the demolition, but only C and the next word are rearranged. Rochdale is a town in Greater Manchester, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rochdale is a town in Greater Manchester in the north of England.

clue.text: Feeling unwell, queen needs a piece of cake?

parts.note: a piece of cake means something easy

explanation.surface: A monarch needs a slice of cake while feeling sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of cake' tempts as a real slice, but the idiom means easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Queasy means nauseous or sick in the stomach.
